# Opcode `0x80` Holdout Provenance Scan

## Goal

Answer the remaining `Pass 5` question left by the residual-context and
template-context packets:

- do the final singleton or variant `0x80` residuals reveal a second
  structural producer
- or do they still collapse back into the already established room-entry,
  cutscene, or state-variant scaffolds

This pass focuses only on the `3` files that were still marked
`singleton_or_variant` in
[`opcode_0x80_template_scan.json`](opcode_0x80_template_scan.json).

## Method

- Start from the checked-in
  [`opcode_0x80_template_scan.json`](opcode_0x80_template_scan.json) output.
- Reclassify only the `singleton_or_variant` rows by:
  - selector-byte reuse against the dominant residual families
  - same-title sibling links already recorded by the residual scan
  - immediate decoded-script context before and after the first `0x80`
- Preserve the result as
  [`opcode_0x80_holdout_scan.json`](opcode_0x80_holdout_scan.json), generated
  by
  [`../verification/analyze_opcode_0x80_holdouts.py`](../verification/analyze_opcode_0x80_holdouts.py).

## Corpus result

The holdout set is now small enough to characterize directly:

- only `3 / 42` residual files were still outside the two repeated paired
  families after the template pass
- `2 / 3` of those holdouts still reuse the dominant `0x41/0x42` selector
  bytes
- the remaining `1 / 3` uses a unique selector byte, but it is also the only
  holdout with a same-title sibling variant that already stages a complete
  pre-burst neighboring sound pair
- none of the `3` holdouts introduce a new complete sound pair before their
  first `0x80`

The wider selector view sharpens that even more:

- `38 / 42` residual records now belong to the `0x41/0x42` selector family
  once the singleton holdouts are included
- `3 / 42` belong to the repeated `0x1D/0x1E` family
- only `1 / 42` residual record is left on any other selector byte at all:
  `0x0E` in `MAP022`

That is not the shape of a second unresolved producer family.

## `021` and `025`: dominant-selector singletons

Two of the three holdouts reduce cleanly to loosened forms of the dominant
`0x41/0x42` family:

- [`021-Room of Rotten Grapes`](../../decoded_scripts/1-Wine%20Cellar/021-Room%20of%20Rotten%20Grapes.txt)
  uses a lone `80 03 41 80 7F`
- [`025-The Hero's Winehall`](../../decoded_scripts/1-Wine%20Cellar/025-The%20Hero's%20Winehall.txt)
  uses a lone `80 01 42 80 7F`

That matters because those are not fresh selector values.
They are the same `0x41` and `0x42` bytes already dominating the `36`-file
paired family; these scenes just reuse them without the usual immediate partner
burst.

Their surrounding context stays structural, not audio-forward:

- `021` places the `0x41` burst directly after splash-screen load/show/fade
  setup, then waits, flips model animations, and continues through camera and
  staging work rather than any complete neighboring sound path
- `025` places the `0x42` burst after `WaitForFile`, `Opcode3D`, and
  `Wait(1)`, then immediately exits through `Opcode43` and `Opcode6E`, which
  reads like a minimal room-state tail instead of a standalone sound action

So these two files widen the already-known dominant family.
They do not create a new one.

## `022`: same-title variant, not a second producer

The last holdout,
[`022-Chamber of Fear (after the quake)`](../../decoded_scripts/1-Wine%20Cellar/022-Chamber%20of%20Fear%20(after%20the%20quake).txt),
is the only residual singleton that does not reuse the dominant selector
family.
Its first burst is `80 03 0E 80 7F`.

Even so, it still does not point to a second structural producer:

- it has no complete neighboring sound pair before the first `0x80`
- its immediate post-burst flow is still cutscene control:
  wait, `Opcode93`, `ScriptCallSlotActive`, first-person toggle, and further
  scripted camera/dialog work
- it is the only holdout with a same-title sibling variant already logged by
  the residual scan:
  [`017-Chamber of Fear`](../../decoded_scripts/1-Wine%20Cellar/017-Chamber%20of%20Fear.txt)
  stages the explicit `0x85/0x88` SFX setup before its own later `0x80`

That makes `022` look more like a state-specific rewrite of the same scene
family than like a new broad producer for inert `0x80` bursts.

## Safe takeaway

- the final holdouts do **not** reveal a second structural producer for
  `0x80`
- `021` and `025` are best treated as singleton or truncated reuse of the
  dominant `0x41/0x42` scaffold family
- `022` is best treated as a same-title state variant case anchored by `017`,
  not as fresh direct-sound evidence
- no remaining residual file currently argues against promoting the structural
  label `Opcode80SharedStub`

This does not explain *why* content-authoring templates kept those inert bursts.
But it does close the narrower campaign blocker:
the remaining singleton and variant holdouts do not force a second semantic
reading for `0x80`.
